title: A matter of waste
paragraphs: Should you recycle the box from your takeaway pizza or throw it away? Can you recycle aerosol cans? Is all plastic recyclable? How clued up about recycling are you?
We probably all know that recycling is good for the environment. It saves energy and limits the drain on Earth's resources. But do you know which items you should or shouldn't recycle?

In the UK, we have a well-established system of kerbside recycling. Most people expect to separate recyclable material from general refuse. A typical household recycles paper, cardboard, plastic and glass bottles, foil and drinks cans. Food and garden waste is now also collected. But in the last four years, the number of items rejected for recycling in England has gone up by 84%, mainly as a result of contamination.
Many items end up in landfill or being incinerated when, with more care, they could be recycled. The problem often stems from confusion over what and how to recycle.

Across the UK the system of recycling differs between local authorities, and multiple containers are used for different types of recyclables. In one area there may be one large wheelie bin for recycling all household items, another for garden waste, and yet another for general waste. There are also composting food caddies - a small one for the kitchen and a larger one for the kerbside. These use compostable bags for food waste, including tea bags, coffee grindings and egg shells. A few streets away, another council may use a separate container just for glass bottles. Waste collection times vary - either weekly or fortnightly. Each week, you have to remember which bin has to go out. It's all highly confusing.

One of the biggest problems recycling firms face is food contamination. If your plastic milk bottle is empty, it's ok to recycle it, but if it contains a small amount of milk, it could result in contamination of the plastic recycling process. Likewise, paper fibres cannot be recycled if they are contaminated with food, so a cheesy pizza box shouldn't be recycled.

Conscientious consumers are constantly faced with recycling conundrums. You've just finished a carton of juice. Should you remove the plastic cap before recycling the carton? You feel the fate of the planet lies in your hands. My advice: stop worrying and crack open a bottle of beer! ...Hang on! ... what should you do with the bottle top?!

vocabulary.entry: recycle [v.] /ˌriːˈsaɪkəl/ 回收利用 (专业词汇)
vocabulary.example: We recycle all our glass and paper.
vocabulary.translation: 我们回收所有的玻璃和纸张。

vocabulary.entry: aerosol can [n.] /ˈeərəsɒl kæn/ 喷雾罐 (专业词汇)
vocabulary.example: Aerosol cans should be disposed of carefully.
vocabulary.translation: 喷雾罐应小心处理。

vocabulary.entry: plastic [n.] /ˈplæstɪk/ 塑料
vocabulary.example: Plastic takes hundreds of years to decompose.
vocabulary.translation: 塑料需要数百年才能分解。

vocabulary.entry: clued up [adj.] /kluːd ʌp/ 了解；熟悉 (英式英语；口语)
vocabulary.example: She is clued up about the latest fashion trends.
vocabulary.translation: 她对最新的时尚潮流很了解。

vocabulary.entry: drain on [phr.] /dreɪn ɒn/ 对……的消耗 (固定搭配)
vocabulary.example: The project was a drain on the company's resources.
vocabulary.translation: 这个项目消耗了公司的资源。

vocabulary.entry: kerbside recycling [n.] /ˈkɜːbsaɪd ˌriːˈsaɪklɪŋ/ 路边回收 (英式拼写，美式: curbside recycling；专业词汇)
vocabulary.example: Kerbside recycling makes it easy for households to recycle.
vocabulary.translation: 路边回收让家庭回收变得容易。

vocabulary.entry: refuse [n.] /ˈrefjuːs/ 垃圾；废弃物 (正式用语)
vocabulary.example: The truck collects household refuse every Tuesday.
vocabulary.translation: 卡车每周二收集家庭垃圾。

vocabulary.entry: foil [n.] /fɔɪl/ 箔纸；锡箔纸
vocabulary.example: Cover the dish with aluminium foil.
vocabulary.translation: 用铝箔纸盖住盘子。

vocabulary.entry: reject [v.] /rɪˈdʒekt/ 拒收；拒绝 (书面语)
vocabulary.example: The factory rejects defective products.
vocabulary.translation: 工厂拒收有缺陷的产品。

vocabulary.entry: contamination [n.] /kənˌtæmɪˈneɪʃən/ 污染 (专业词汇)
vocabulary.example: The water supply was closed due to contamination.
vocabulary.translation: 由于污染，供水被关闭。

vocabulary.entry: landfill [n.] /ˈlændfɪl/ 垃圾填埋场 (专业词汇)
vocabulary.example: Much of our waste ends up in landfill.
vocabulary.translation: 我们的许多垃圾最终被填埋。

vocabulary.entry: incinerate [v.] /ɪnˈsɪnəreɪt/ 焚烧 (专业词汇)
vocabulary.example: The waste is incinerated at a high temperature.
vocabulary.translation: 废物在高温下被焚烧。

vocabulary.entry: stem from [phr.] /stem frɒm/ 源于；来自 (固定搭配)
vocabulary.example: The problem stems from a lack of communication.
vocabulary.translation: 这个问题源于缺乏沟通。

vocabulary.entry: wheelie bin [n.] /ˈwiːli bɪn/ 有轮大垃圾桶 (英式英语；口语)
vocabulary.example: Put the rubbish in the wheelie bin.
vocabulary.translation: 把垃圾放进有轮大垃圾桶。

vocabulary.entry: composting [n.] /ˈkɒmpɒstɪŋ/ 堆肥 (专业词汇)
vocabulary.example: Composting turns food waste into fertilizer.
vocabulary.translation: 堆肥将食物垃圾转化为肥料。

vocabulary.entry: caddy [n.] /ˈkædi/ 小桶；小容器
vocabulary.example: She keeps tea in a caddy.
vocabulary.translation: 她把茶叶放在茶叶罐里。

vocabulary.entry: compostable [adj.] /kɒmˈpɒstəbəl/ 可堆肥的 (专业词汇)
vocabulary.example: These bags are made of compostable materials.
vocabulary.translation: 这些袋子由可堆肥材料制成。

vocabulary.entry: likewise [adv.] /ˈlaɪkwaɪz/ 同样地 (正式用语)
vocabulary.example: He is friendly, and likewise his brother.
vocabulary.translation: 他很友好，他的兄弟也同样。

vocabulary.entry: cheesy [adj.] /ˈtʃiːzi/ 有奶酪的；俗气的 (口语)
vocabulary.example: I don't like this cheesy pizza.
vocabulary.translation: 我不喜欢这个有奶酪的披萨。

vocabulary.entry: conscientious [adj.] /ˌkɒnʃiˈenʃəs/ 认真负责的；有良知的
vocabulary.example: She is a conscientious worker.
vocabulary.translation: 她是一个认真负责的工人。

vocabulary.entry: conundrum [n.] /kəˈnʌndrəm/ 难题；复杂的问题 (书面语)
vocabulary.example: This is a difficult conundrum to solve.
vocabulary.translation: 这是一个难以解决的难题。

sentences.english: Many items end up in landfill or being incinerated when, with more care, they could be recycled.

sentences.chinese: 如果你的塑料牛奶瓶是空的，那么可以回收它，但如果里面还有少量牛奶，就可能会导致塑料回收过程受到污染。

sentences.chinese: 在回收纸盒之前，你应该把塑料盖子拿掉吗？
